paper.title: Best Arm Identification in Restless Markov Multi-Armed Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Best arm identification in restless Markov multi-armed bandits (TPMs known up to permutation)
unmapped: Each arm is a time-homogeneous ergodic Markov chain on a common finite state space; unselected arms keep evolving (restless)
The learner knows the set of TPMs P_1..P_K but not their assignment to arms (finite hypothesis set of permutations)
Best arm = arm with largest stationary mean of a known function f
Rows of the TPMs are mutually absolutely continuous across arms
Initial states drawn from a distribution phi independent of the assignment
Learner observes the full state of the selected arm
settings.definition_quote: A decision entity that knows $P_1, \ldots, P_K$ only up to a permutation wishes to find the index of the best arm (i.e., the arm whose TPM is $P_1$) as quickly as possible, subject to an upper bound on the error probability.

symbols.T_star: T*(C): sup over state-action occupancy measures nu on (delays, last observed states, arm) of min over alternatives C' of sum nu * KL between d-step transition rows

conditions: policies in Pi(epsilon): error probability <= epsilon for all assignments

source.label: prop:lower_bound
source.quote: Suppose $C\in \mathcal{C}$ is the underlying assignment of the TPMs. Then, \liminf_{\epsilon\downarrow 0}\inf_{\pi\in\Pi(\epsilon)}\frac{\mathbb{E}_{C}^\pi[\tau(\pi)]}{\log(1/\epsilon)}\geq \frac{1}{T^{\star}(C)}

results.notes: Paper's epsilon is the error probability (delta). Restated as first part of Theorem 4.

source.label: lem:pi_star(L)_in_Pi(epsilon)
source.quote: Fix an error probability threshold $\epsilon>0$. If $L=1/\epsilon$, then $\pi^\star(L,\eta,R)\in\Pi(\epsilon)$ for all $\eta\in (0,1]$ and $R\in \mathbb{N}\cap (K, \infty)$.

results.notes: delta-correctness of the policy: error probability at most epsilon. Compute: paper calls it practically implementable (finite state space S_R) but per-round cost involves enumerating permutations.

symbols.eta_mix: mixing weight eta in (0,1] between uniform and optimal occupancy measures
symbols.T_R_unif: min over alternatives of KL-weighted sum under the uniform delay-constrained occupancy measure
symbols.T_R_star: optimal value of the finite LP with maximum delay R

source.label: Lemma:almost_sure_upper_bound_for_policy_pi_star
source.quote: Fix $\eta\in (0,1]$, $R\in \mathbb{N}\cap(K, \infty)$, and $C\in \mathcal{C}$. Under the assignment of the TPMs $C$ and under the policy $\pi=\pi^*(L,\eta, R)$, \limsup_{L\to\infty}\, \frac{\tau(\pi)}{\log L} \leq ... \leq \frac{1}{\eta\,T_{R}^{\textsf{unif}}(C) + (1-\eta)\ T_{R}^{\star}(C)} almost surely

results.notes: Almost-sure bound on stopping time, expressed with log L = log(1/delta).

symbols.T_R_unif: min over alternatives of KL-weighted sum under the uniform delay-constrained occupancy measure
symbols.T_R_star: optimal value of the finite LP with maximum delay R

source.label: prop:upper_bound
source.quote: Fix $\eta\in (0,1]$, $R\in \mathbb{N}\cap (K, \infty)$, and $C\in \mathcal{C}$. Under the assignment of the TPMs $C$, the policy {\sc $R$-DCR-BAI} satisfies \limsup_{L\to\infty}\frac{\mathbb{E}_{C}^{\pi}[\tau(\pi)]}{\log L}\leq \frac{1}{\eta\,T_{R}^{\textsf{unif}}(C) + (1-\eta)\ T_{R}^{\star}(C)}.

results.notes: With L = 1/epsilon the policy is epsilon-correct (Lemma 3).

bound.regime: L -> infinity, then eta -> 0, then R -> infinity

source.label: prop:main_result
source.quote: Further, given any $\epsilon>0$, the policy $\pi^{\star}(1/\epsilon, \eta, R) \in \Pi(\epsilon)$ for all $\eta\in (0,1]$ and $R\in \mathbb{N}\cap (K, \infty)$. Additionally, \limsup_{R\to\infty}\ \limsup_{\eta \downarrow 0} \ \limsup_{L\to\infty}\ \frac{\mathbb{E}_{C}^{\pi^\star(L, \eta, R)}[\tau(\pi^\star(L, \eta, R))]}{\log L}\leq \frac{1}{\lim_{R\to\infty}\ T_{R}^{\star}(C)}

results.notes: Theorem 4 also restates the lower bound of Proposition 1 (r1). By Lemma 7, when each TPM has identical rows (i.i.d. case) T_R*(C)=T*(C) for all R, so upper and lower bounds match. For fixed R, the bound with eta->0 is 1/T_R*(C).
